A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPLA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original value-system construction, factor analyses, safety prediction, alignment experiments, and lexicon-coverage analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, and adds correlations with Schwartz’s four higher-level values.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same agents, frequency-based lexicon filtering, GPV measurement, and PCA construction. The BaseAlign adaptation, target-distillation objective, and PPO alignment procedure also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four lexicon sources, SALAD-Bench safety tasks, LMSYS-Chat-1M coverage evaluation, and preference-based alignment tasks. No dataset, language, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The appendix correlation comparison expands from Schwartz’s ten values in v1 Table 12 to also include its four higher-level dimensions in v4 Table 11. Comparator membership in the main CFA, safety-prediction, and alignment experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The 33-model-by-21-prompt subject design, 123 elicitation prompts, CFA construction/holdout split, 512-conversation coverage sample, and alignment settings remain unchanged. The new aggregate correlation table does not establish revised sampling or experimental protocols; omission of the printed anchoring prompts is a documentation change.

E4.justification: v4 Table 11 extends the existing cross-system correlation analysis to Schwartz’s four higher-level dimensions, supporting the added discussion of anchoring bias. Existing circumplex, cross-dataset consistency, lexicon-coverage, safety-contribution, and ValueLex analyses are retained. No direct comparison across anchoring conditions is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% Cronbach’s-alpha confidence intervals, the same uncertainty notation for safety accuracy, and the same CFA bootstrapping description. Revised endpoints for one confidence interval change a result, without establishing a change in statistical procedures, run counts, or reporting practices.

E6.justification: Self-Competence’s confidence interval changes from 0.346–0.481 to 0.732–0.787, while alpha remains 0.761, in the main and full loading tables. v4 Table 11 adds 20 higher-level Schwartz correlations, including Risk-Taking–Conservation at -0.688. Main benchmark scores, factor loadings, alignment targets, and previously reported correlations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical models and derivations in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. The new anchoring-bias discussion offers conceptual reasoning, without adding formal assumptions, mathematical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: GPLA, the five-factor LLM value system, and three benchmarking tasks. Claims of psychological grounding and superior validity and utility over Schwartz’s values retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly argues that Schwartz-based anchoring prompts do not bias the recovered structure, invoking psychological precedent and cross-system correlations. It also newly characterizes those correlations as only weak to moderate. Existing factor interpretations and limitations concerning English-only measurement and a single alignment target remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes v1 Table 7’s complete anchoring-prompt list; Appendix A.2 instead supplies the default prompt and cites the remaining 20 prompts. Appendix A.1 replaces exact data-file and subset links with repository or dataset roots. Other documented model, hardware, question-generation, and alignment details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cieciuch et al. (2014) and Tevrüz et al. (2015) to support its anchoring argument, Ye et al. (2025a) on LLM psychometrics, and Zhu et al. (2023) for the default prompt. Several background references, including Bardi et al. (2008) and Demszky et al. (2023), disappear. The central positioning against ValueLex remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v1’s Section 4 validation and advantages discussion becomes v4’s Section 6 after the results. Detailed factor interpretations move from the main results into Appendix B.3, replaced by a compact summary. Background passages are condensed and citations switch to author–year style.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to predominantly two-column layout. Table 1 is condensed and restructured, Table 2 is transposed, the anchoring-prompt table disappears, and a higher-level correlation table is added. Existing figures are repositioned, and the full loading table moves to the document’s end.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the inconsistent Self-Competence interval and adds useful correlation results, but removes exact anchoring prompts and precise data locations. Its new claim that anchoring cannot bias structure lacks a comparison across anchoring conditions; the accompanying description of correlations as only weak to moderate also sits uneasily with a magnitude of 0.779 in Table 10. These gains in numerical reporting and losses in reproducibility and interpretive caution leave the net quality direction uncertain.
